From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — Dedicated GPU capacity for Acme Health

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we agreed on. Let me know if I missed anything.

TL;DR: Acme needs dedicated, isolated capacity for production inference (primary use: multi-tenant inference for clinical summarization) with predictable throughput and strict networking isolation.

Key pain points you described:
- Unpredictable latency and token costs on shared endpoints during spikes (affects clinician workflows).
- Regulatory requirement: workloads must run inside an Acme VPC or equivalent isolated environment (no shared networking).
- Need clear SLAs (uptime and latency p95 targets) and auditability for audit logs.

Goals we captured:
- Start with a 3-month pilot: 50–100 A100-equivalent reserved units; scale to 200 over 6–9 months if performance and cost targets are met.
- p95 latency target: <150ms for 512-token average inference.
- Uptime SLO target: 99.9% with clear failure modes and fallbacks.
- Data control: option for Redwood Private (VPC or colocated on AWS account) to satisfy procurement/security.

Recommended Redwood configuration (high-level):
1) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with private VPC peering to Acme or Redwood Private in Acme AWS account — final choice depends on procurement and security review.
2) Autoscaling policy: baseline reserved capacity for steady-state throughput + burst pool (preemptible capacity) for spikes.
3) KV/prefix caching enabled for common prompts to reduce per-token cost.
4) Monitoring: per-route latency & cost dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs for requests.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Logan: send capacity worksheet and a draft MOU (attached) to capture sizing assumptions and commercial terms — DONE (attachments).
- Jordan: confirm preferred isolation model (VPC peering vs Redwood-managed Private deployment) and procurement timeline.
- Marissa & Vivek: prepare a technical deep-dive for networking and SSO (tentative call week of 11/10).
- Redwood: provide a firm 90-day pilot price and a one-page SLA summary.

Attachments: capacity_worksheet.xlsx (sizing assumptions + example pricing), redwood-mou-draft.pdf (draft MOU / pilot terms).

Proposed timeline:
- 11/6: Redwood to deliver formal pilot quote and one-page SLA.
- 11/12 (or week of 11/10): technical deep-dive with Vivek + Acme infra.
- Mid-Nov: procurement review / signature for pilot.

If that aligns, I’ll put the 11/12 slot on the calendar and get Marissa and Vivek prepped.

Thanks — Logan

Thanks Logan — this is helpful, appreciate the clear bullets. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Capacity: the 50–100 A100-equivalent range sounds right for the pilot. Can you break that into steady-state vs burst in the worksheet? Our typical pattern is 8–10k requests/day but unpredictable afternoon spikes.

2) Isolation: procurement will push for anything that lets us keep keys and logs inside our AWS account. Is the Redwood Private option something you deploy into our VPC (we manage), or is it a managed service still controlled by Redwood? Need this clarified before legal signs off.

3) Budget & timing: we have $120k–$150k allocated for the pilot in Q4 procurement. Can you confirm a firm quote that lands in that band (including any setup/ingest costs)? Priya is on copy and will handle the procurement steps.

4) SLA: 99.9% for availability is what we expect — can you tell me what penalties or credits are typical? Also want to confirm fallback behavior if dedicated pool is saturated (does Redwood automatically route to a compatible hosted instance or reject?).

We’re generally aligned, and Priya will coordinate internal approvals if the isolation model and pricing look good.

On the technical call: week of 11/10 works — earliest availability for our infra team would be 11/12 in the afternoon PST.

-Jordan
CTO, Acme Health

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Dedicated GPU capacity for Acme Health

Jordan — great to meet earlier. Quick answers to your questions and a proposed technical approach.

On isolation: Redwood has two paths that match your ask: 
- Redwood Private (preferred for strict controls): we deploy a private control plane and runtime into your AWS account (we can support a template-based CloudFormation / Terraform deployment you operate). This gives you keys and logs in your account and satisfies most procurement concerns.
- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed): reserved GPU pools hosted in a Redwood VPC with peering options. We can offer tighter network controls, but keys and audit logs remain on Redwood’s control plane (we can provide streamed logs and audit exports).

On SLAs and fallbacks:
- Baseline SLA options: 99.5% / 99.9% / 99.95% for availability (pilot typically starts at 99.5% and we upgrade post-contract). Credits scale with severity; I’ll attach the one-pager SLA summary in the formal quote.
- Fallback behavior: we can configure automatic fallback to a hosted model variant (configurable) or queue/reject requests when dedicated pool is saturated. For clinical workflows you described, we recommend fallback to a compatible, lower-cost model with throttling rather than outright rejects.

On pricing & timeline:
- We’ll deliver a firm pilot quote that includes a line for setup (infra deployment + security review) and a monthly reserved capacity fee. I’ll work with Logan to make sure the pilot price targets the $120k–$150k band you noted.

Vivek — looping you in to schedule the deep-dive on networking, VPC templates, and SSO. Jordan / Priya — can you confirm whether Acme prefers Redwood to deploy into a customer-managed CloudFormation/Terraform template or if you want Redwood to manage the environment? That will materially affect setup timing.

Next steps (concrete):
- Redwood: formal pilot quote + SLA one-pager (by 11/6) — Logan / Marissa
- Acme: decision on deployment model (customer-managed deployment template vs Redwood-managed private deployment) — Jordan / Priya
- Schedule technical deep-dive: target 11/12 afternoon PST — Vivek to lead.

Thanks — Marissa
